stories.headline: RBI proposes optional 'trusted person' check on big bank transfers
stories.question: Will a 'trusted person' soon have to approve some of my UPI or bank transfers?
stories.dek: Only if you choose it. The RBI's 23 November draft lets you name someone to approve large transfers. Ordinary UPI payments are reportedly excluded, and most rules would start on 1 July 2027.

so_far.text: Online fraud is a growing worry in India. The Supreme Court has flagged losses of about ₹52,000 crore from cyber fraud and 'digital arrest' scams, where callers pose as officials and scare people into paying. During 2026 the court has pushed the government, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and banks to flag suspicious transactions and protect victims. The RBI first floated ideas in a discussion paper. Some of those ideas appear again in the new draft.

what_happened.text: On 23 November 2026 the RBI issued draft directions with two new tools. The first is a 'Trusted Person Mechanism'. You nominate someone aged 18 or over to approve your electronic transfers above an amount you set. They get one hour. If they reject the transfer or don't reply, it fails. This tool is voluntary. The Tribune reports that UPI, merchant and recurring payments are excluded. The second tool is a 'Stop Switch', which lets you block new debits you start, new mandates and UPI sign-ups on new apps. The draft also widens when a bank counts as negligent in fraud cases. Comments are due by 14 December 2026.

steps.text: Scams like digital arrest work by rushing one frightened person into paying before anyone else can check.
Once money moves electronically, it can be spread across accounts within minutes, so getting it back is hard.
So the RBI's draft adds a second approver for large transfers, giving up to one hour and an outside view.
A scammer must now fool two people. If the trusted person rejects or stays silent, the transfer fails.
The separate Stop Switch lets you block new debits you start, new mandates and UPI sign-ups on new apps.

history.text:
This story starts in the Supreme Court. In February 2026 the court was hearing a case on digital-arrest and cyber frauds. It told the Centre to draft SOPs (fixed step-by-step procedures) with the RBI and banks. The SOPs were meant to flag suspicious transactions. The court also asked them to explore compensation for victims.

The RBI then published a discussion paper, an early set of ideas for public comment. It floated a one-hour delay on transfers above ₹10,000 and a kill switch. It also floated trusted-person approval above ₹50,000 for people aged 70 or over or with disabilities. Comments closed on 8 May 2026. This was the first sketch of the tools now proposed.

On 4 August 2026 the court gave the RBI four weeks to adopt an SOP. Under it, banks could put temporary debit holds on accounts linked to cyber fraud.

On 29 October 2026 the court said it would examine the RBI's proposed anti-fraud rules before they are notified. It pressed for safeguards against unusual transactions and for compensation from banks.

On 23 November 2026 the RBI issued its draft directions. The trusted-person threshold is now set by each customer, not fixed at one amount. It is not yet known whether this is the draft the court will examine.

analogy.text: Think of a shop where any bill above a set amount needs the manager's signature. The cashier still handles small sales alone. A con artist who rushes the cashier now has to fool the manager too. If the manager doesn't sign, there is no sale.
analogy.breaks: The trusted person can only say yes or no. They can't see your account, and UPI and merchant payments skip the check.

for_you.text: Nothing changes for now. If you worry about scam calls, for example on behalf of older parents, you could later name a trusted person to approve big bank transfers above a limit you choose. This would start from 1 July 2027, or earlier if your bank adopts it. Everyday UPI and shop payments would reportedly not be affected. Anyone can send comments to the RBI until 14 December 2026.

misconception.fact: The draft mechanism is voluntary and needs both people's consent. The Tribune reports it excludes UPI, merchant and recurring payments.

lesson.concept: How a second approver stops a rushed transfer
lesson.big_idea: Most payment scams work by rushing one person, alone, into sending money. A second approver for large transfers adds a pause and a fresh pair of eyes, so the scammer must fool two people.

steps.title: Scams rely on rush
steps.text: In a scam like digital arrest, a caller frightens you and keeps you on the line. The goal is to make you pay before you can think or ask anyone.

steps.title: A threshold sorts payments
steps.text: You pick an amount, called the threshold. Transfers below it go through as normal. Transfers above it wait for a second yes. In the RBI draft, you set this amount yourself.

steps.title: A trusted person says yes
steps.text: You name someone aged 18 or over. They get one hour to approve. If they reject, or say nothing, the transfer fails. They get no access to your account and aren't liable.

steps.title: Some payments skip the check
steps.text: The Tribune reports that UPI, merchant payments and recurring ones are excluded. Recurring ones include e-mandates, standing permissions for regular debits like EMIs. A separate Stop Switch can block new debits you start.

steps.title: Both must agree first
steps.text: The system is voluntary. You and the trusted person must both consent. Then the bank waits a 24-hour cooling-off period, a fixed pause, before switching it on.

example.setup: Imagine Asha, 72, names her daughter Meera as her trusted person and sets her threshold at ₹25,000. Then a caller posing as police demands ₹3 lakh by bank transfer.

lines.label: Small transfer
lines.note: Under the threshold, so it goes straight through.

lines.label: Scam transfer
lines.note: Over the threshold, so it waits for Meera.

lines.label: Meera's window
lines.calc: One hour to approve or reject
lines.note: She calls Asha and recognises the scam.

lines.label: Meera rejects
lines.calc: Rejected, so ₹3 lakh stays with Asha
lines.note: Had Meera not replied, the transfer would also fail.

example.result: Small everyday transfers aren't slowed down. Only large ones wait, and both a 'no' and silence keep the money safe. The scammer has to fool two people, not one.

apply.text: That is the design of the RBI's 23 November 2026 draft. You choose the threshold and the trusted person, who gets one hour. But The Tribune reports UPI payments are excluded, so Meera would not be asked about an ordinary UPI transfer. The Stop Switch, a separate tool, can block new customer-initiated debits and new UPI app registrations.

practice.q: Asha keeps her ₹25,000 threshold. She sends ₹20,000 by bank transfer, ₹60,000 by bank transfer and ₹60,000 by UPI. Which needs Meera's approval?
practice.answer: Check each one. ₹20,000 is below ₹25,000, so it goes straight through. ₹60,000 by bank transfer is above ₹25,000, so Meera must approve within one hour. ₹60,000 by UPI is above the threshold, but UPI is reportedly excluded, so no approval is asked. Only one payment needs Meera.

terms.meaning: An opt-in rule where someone you name approves your large electronic transfers.

check.q: You set a ₹1 lakh threshold. Your trusted person ignores a ₹2 lakh bank-transfer request for an hour. What happens?
options: The transfer goes through automatically
The transfer fails
The bank decides instead
check.why: Under the draft, a rejection or no reply within one hour means the transfer fails, so silence protects your money.

takeaways: A second approver on large transfers means a scammer must fool two people, not one.
The RBI's 23 November draft makes this optional; UPI and merchant payments are reportedly excluded.
Comments close on 14 December 2026; most safeguards would apply from 1 July 2027.

scenes.say: Kya jald hi aapke UPI ya bank transfers ko kisi aur ka approval chahiye hoga? 23 November 2026 ko Reserve Bank of India ne ek naya anti-fraud check propose kiya. Chaliye dekhte hain yeh kya karta hai, aur kya nahi.

scenes.say: Hua yeh ki 23 November 2026 ko Reserve Bank ne draft rules jaari kiye. Draft matlab proposal, abhi final nahi. Bada idea hai Trusted Person Mechanism. Aap 18 saal ya usse zyada umar ke kisi insaan ko chunte hain, jo aapke chune hue amount se upar ke electronic transfers approve karega.
scenes.speak: हुआ यह कि 23 November 2026 को Reserve Bank ने draft rules जारी किए। Draft मतलब proposal, अभी final नहीं। बड़ा idea है Trusted Person Mechanism। आप 18 साल या उससे ज़्यादा उमर के किसी इंसान को चुनते हैं, जो आपके चुने हुए amount से ऊपर के electronic transfers approve करेगा।

scenes.say: Us insaan ke paas 1 ghanta hota hai. Agar woh reject kare, ya jawab na de, toh transfer fail. Ek Stop Switch bhi hai. Yeh aapke shuru kiye naye debits, naye mandates aur naye apps par UPI sign-ups block karta hai, lekin pehle se chal rahe auto-debits aur aane wala paisa chalta rehta hai. Draft yeh bhi badhata hai ki fraud mein bank kab negligent maane jayenge.
scenes.show: One hour to approve. Plus a Stop Switch.
scenes.speak: उस इंसान के पास 1 घंटा होता है। अगर वह reject करे, या जवाब न दे, तो transfer fail। एक Stop Switch भी है। यह आपके शुरू किए नए debits, नए mandates और नए apps पर UPI sign-ups block करता है, लेकिन पहले से चल रहे auto-debits और आने वाला पैसा चलता रहता है। Draft यह भी बढ़ाता है कि fraud में bank कब negligent माने जाएंगे।

scenes.say: Toh hamare sawaal ka chhota jawab. Aap par koi zabardasti nahi thopa jayega. Trusted-person scheme voluntary hai, aur aap dono ki sahmati zaroori hai. Aur The Tribune ke mutabik, aam UPI payments, dukaan ki payments aur regular auto-debits isse bahar hain.
scenes.speak: तो हमारे सवाल का छोटा जवाब। आप पर कोई ज़बरदस्ती नहीं थोपा जाएगा। Trusted-person scheme voluntary है, और आप दोनों की सहमति ज़रूरी है। और The Tribune के मुताबिक, आम UPI payments, दुकान की payments और regular auto-debits इससे बाहर हैं।

scenes.say: Yahan tak pahunche kaise? Kahani Supreme Court se shuru hoti hai. February 2026 mein, digital-arrest aur cyber fraud ke ek case ki sunvai mein, court ne government se kaha ki Reserve Bank aur banks ke saath milkar step-by-step procedures draft kare. Maksad: suspicious transactions ko flag karna, aur victims ko paisa lautane ke tareeke dhoondhna.
scenes.speak: यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? कहानी Supreme Court से शुरू होती है। February 2026 में, digital-arrest और cyber fraud के एक case की सुनवाई में, court ने government से कहा कि Reserve Bank और banks के साथ मिलकर step-by-step procedures draft करे। मकसद: suspicious transactions को flag करना, और victims को पैसा लौटाने के तरीके ढूँढना।

scenes.say: Phir Reserve Bank ne public comment ke liye ek discussion paper nikala. Usmein sujhav tha: 10 hazaar rupaye se upar ke transfers par 1 ghante ki delay, ek kill switch, aur 70 saal ya usse zyada umar ke ya disabled logon ke liye 50 hazaar rupaye se upar trusted-person approval. scenes.say: Phir court ne aur dabaav banaya. 4 August 2026 ko usne Reserve Bank ko 4 hafte diye, taaki fraud se jude accounts par banks debits rok sakein, aisa procedure apnaya jaye. 29 October ko court ne kaha ki anti-fraud rules official hone se pehle woh unhe jaanchega. stories.headline: India's business activity rises as S&P expects a December RBI hike
stories.question: Is India's economy strong enough to take another RBI rate hike in December?
stories.dek: Business activity hit a five-month high in November, which points to strong demand. S&P Global Ratings, citing price risks such as weak rain and El Niño, expects a 25 bps hike.

so_far.text: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee sets the repo rate, the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks. On 7 October 2026 it raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. It was the first hike since February 2023, and the RBI called its stance 'calibrated tightening'. Consumer inflation was 6.1% in October, above the RBI's target band of 2–6%. The committee next meets on 2–4 December 2026.

what_happened.text: On 23 November, HSBC's flash composite PMI rose to 56.3 for November, from 56.2 in October. The flash PMI is an early monthly survey of business managers. Firstpost called it a five-month high. Stronger factory demand and output offset slower growth in services. Mint reported demand improving at the quickest rate since June. In an outlook released on 22 November, S&P Global Ratings projected 7% growth in 2026–27 and 2027–28, cutting the 2027–28 figure by 0.2 points. It expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points in December.

steps.text: October inflation of 6.1% sits above the RBI's 2–6% band, which puts pressure on the RBI to act.
At 5.50%, the repo rate is below inflation, so borrowing is still cheap once rising prices are counted.

A hike hurts less when demand is strong, and November's flash PMI rose to a five-month high.
S&P bases its December hike call on price risks: costs passed to shoppers, weak summer rain, low reservoirs and El Niño.

history.text:
The story starts in February 2023. That month the RBI raised its repo rate, and it did not raise it again for more than three and a half years.

A second thread is about how India measures its economy. In late 2025 the IMF gave India's national accounts, the official GDP figures, a 'C' grade. In February 2026 India replaced its 2011–12 GDP series with a new one built on 2022–23. A base year is the reference year the figures are built on. An old base can miss newer parts of the economy. MoSPI, the statistics ministry, also plans to move its next revision to the UN's SNA 2025 rules, which count data as an asset.

By autumn 2026, prices were the worry. On 7 October the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, ending the long pause. Inflation still reached 6.1% in October, above the RBI's 2–6% band. That is why November's growth signals matter: they show whether the economy can bear another hike.

lesson.concept: How the real interest rate shows if money is cheap
lesson.big_idea: An interest rate shows the true cost of money only after you subtract inflation. If the rate is below inflation, borrowing is cheap, so a central bank raises rates to cool prices.

steps.title: The headline rate
steps.text: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks. Banks build their loan and deposit rates on top of it. India's repo rate has been 5.50% since 7 October 2026.

steps.title: Inflation eats into money
steps.text: Inflation is how fast prices rise. At 6% inflation, shopping that cost ₹100 a year ago costs ₹106 now. The RBI aims to keep inflation between 2% and 6%; October's reading was 6.1%.

steps.title: Real rate: rate minus inflation
steps.text: Subtract inflation from the interest rate and you get the real interest rate. It shows what borrowing truly costs, and what saving truly earns, once rising prices are counted.

steps.title: Below zero means cheap money
steps.text: When the real rate is negative, borrowing costs less than prices rise. People and firms borrow and spend more, which can keep prices climbing. Raising the repo rate pushes the real rate back up.

steps.title: Strong demand makes room
steps.text: Raising rates slows spending a little. A central bank finds that easier when demand is strong, because the economy can absorb the slowdown. Weak demand makes a hike riskier.

practice.q: Suppose the repo rate rises to an assumed 6% and inflation averages 5.3%, S&P's forecast for 2026–27. What is the real rate, and is money still cheap?
practice.answer: Real rate = 6% − 5.3% = 0.7%. That is above zero. Borrowing now costs a little more than prices rise, so money is no longer cheap in real terms. Remember: only the 5.3% is a forecast; the 6% rate is an assumption.

stories.headline: Report says voters' Form 6 data was exposed on EC portal
stories.question: Was voters' personal data exposed on the Election Commission's portal, and what is the EC doing?
stories.dek: A report cited by The Hindu says Form 6 voter data was exposed on the Election Commission's portal. The scale and the Commission's response are unknown. Separately, the Supreme Court reordered Bengal's voter-roll appeals.

so_far.text: The Election Commission (EC) runs India's voter rolls. It has been carrying out an SIR, a special recheck of who is on those rolls. In West Bengal, about 38.1 lakh appeals against deletions and inclusions went to special appeal tribunals, and the Supreme Court has been overseeing them. Since 22 January 2026 the EC has run ECINet, one platform that absorbed older apps such as Voter Helpline and cVIGIL. In October 2026 a Charchagram audit looked at who can switch on access to form details on ECINet.

what_happened.text: On 23 November 2026, The Hindu reported, citing a report, that personal data voters submitted through Form 6, the application to join the voter roll, was exposed on the EC's citizen service portal. The headline presents this as a claim. What data, how many records and for how long are not known, nor whether the EC has confirmed or denied it. The same day, the Supreme Court told West Bengal's SIR appeal tribunals to hear deleted voters' appeals first and defer appeals against inclusions. DD News reported the EC launched a KYC feature on ECINet to help voters check candidates' backgrounds.

steps.text: Form 6 holds the personal details people give to join the voter roll, and they reach the EC through online portals.
ECINet now folds many apps into one platform, so more depends on its rules about who can see what.
A report says Form 6 data was visible on the EC's portal; how, how much and for how long are unknown.
An October 2026 audit already found select officials could switch state-wise access to form details, so access rules were being examined.
Separately, deleted voters filed fewer than one in five Bengal appeals; the Supreme Court has now put them first.

history.text:
Worries about the EC's websites are not new. In 2021 a researcher found the EC's voter portal could reveal registered phone numbers. CERT-In, India's national cyber-security response team, alerted the EC on 15 December 2021, and the flaw was patched.

On 22 January 2026 the EC unveiled ECINet at Bharat Mandapam, Delhi. It folded older apps, including the KYC App, Voter Helpline, cVIGIL and Suvidha, into one platform, so more now sits in one place. In April 2026 the EC promoted ECINet's KYC module, which shows candidates' criminal cases, assets and liabilities, education and social media handles.

Meanwhile, West Bengal's SIR appeals reached the Supreme Court. In April 2026 it refused interim voting rights to deleted voters with pending appeals, but let those who won before cut-off dates be added. In an August 2026 hearing, about 7 lakh of roughly 38.1 lakh appeals were from deleted voters; the Court asked the EC to sort the pending appeals.

In September 2026 the Indian Express reported that Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi objected that Form 6 could not be changed without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The EC said Form 6 itself was never amended. In October 2026 a civic-tech audit by Charchagram found ECINet features letting select officials switch state-wise access to enumeration form details on and off. The 23 November report about Form 6 data lands on top of all this.

lesson.concept: How a portal decides who sees your data
lesson.big_idea: A safe portal asks two questions every time: who are you, and is this record yours? Many data exposures happen when the second question is skipped.

steps.title: Every record has a number
steps.text: A portal stores each form in a database, a large organised table of records. Each form gets a reference number so the system can find it. If numbers run in order, the next one is easy to guess.

steps.title: Logging in proves who you are
steps.text: When you enter a password or a one-time password (OTP), the portal confirms your identity. This is called authentication. It answers only one question: are you really the person you claim to be?

steps.title: Then check the record is yours
steps.text: Each time you ask for a record, the server should check that it belongs to you. This is called authorisation. Without it, anyone who has logged in can ask for any number and get it.

steps.title: Automation multiplies one mistake
steps.text: A small program can send many requests a second, changing the number each time. So one missing check, plus guessable numbers, can expose a whole database in hours rather than years.

steps.title: The fix is a rule, every time
steps.text: Fixes include checking ownership on every request, using random reference numbers, and limiting how fast requests can come. In 2021 a phone-number flaw on the EC's voter portal was patched after CERT-In alerted the EC on 15 December.

example.setup: Imagine a portal holding 1,00,000 forms, numbered 1 to 1,00,000. You log in with an OTP and open your own form, number 50,000.

lines.label: Your form
lines.note: You passed authentication with your OTP.

lines.label: Change one digit
lines.note: A curious or harmful user tries the next number.

lines.label: No ownership check
lines.note: The server never asked whether the form is yours.

lines.label: Script speed
lines.note: A simple program can do this automatically.

lines.label: Time to copy all
lines.note: The whole database, in under three hours.

lines.label: With ownership check
lines.note: Only your own form ever loads.

example.result: One skipped check turned 1,00,000 private forms into something a stranger could copy in under three hours. Adding the ownership check brings that to zero.

apply.text: It is not yet known how the Form 6 data was exposed, how many records were involved, or for how long. But this lesson gives the right questions for the EC: who could see the data, was ownership checked, and has it been fixed, as the 2021 phone-number flaw was after CERT-In's alert.

practice.q: The same kind of portal holds 50,000 forms but allows only 1 request per second. With no ownership check, how long to copy them all?
practice.answer: Requests needed: 50,000. Speed: 1 per second. Time: 50,000 ÷ 1 = 50,000 seconds. Divide by 3,600 seconds in an hour: about 13.9 hours. Slower, but still under a day. With an ownership check, a stranger gets zero forms.

thread.previously: COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, needs consensus. The 19 November draft dropped all fossil-fuel transition language, kept 35% electrification by 2035 and 1.5C, and replaced the earlier $120bn adaptation figure with "at least triple by 2035". Panama threatens to object without eight conditions. India and the Like-Minded Developing Countries oppose the electrification target in the cover decision; India is undecided on the pledge. As of 21 November talks were in overtime with no deal; only technical matters passed.
thread.changed: On 22 November COP31 formally ended without its main decision. Oil producers blocked fossil-fuel wording; the EU, UK and vulnerable states rejected the weakened draft. Paris and Dubai commitments stand; some smaller decisions survive.

stories.headline: COP31 climate summit in Antalya ends without a main deal
stories.question: Why did the COP31 climate talks collapse, and what happens to climate action now?
stories.dek: UN climate deals need every country's consent. Oil producers blocked fossil-fuel wording; the EU and others rejected a text without it. So COP31 ended with no main deal, though Paris still stands.

so_far.text: COP31, the yearly UN climate summit, met in Antalya, Türkiye, under President Murat Kurum. Every decision needs consensus. After objections from Saudi Arabia and other oil producers, a second draft removed all mention of fossil fuels. The EU warned this risked a 'fossil summit'. Panama and about a dozen nations threatened to leave. Before the collapse, India said it did not want firm targets.

what_happened.text: On 22 November 2026, COP31 ended without adopting its main political decision. Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas. The EU, the UK and climate-vulnerable states rejected the final draft as too weak. COP31 President Murat Kurum said the drafts failed for lack of consensus. The talks broke down two days after their scheduled end, the longest in the summit's history. Al Jazeera called it the first collapse without a final deal in 17 years. No roadmap for the 2023 Dubai commitment was agreed.

steps.text: UN climate decisions need consensus, so a single country's objection can block a whole deal.
Saudi Arabia and other oil producers objected to any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas.
To win them over, the second draft removed every mention of fossil fuels.
The EU, UK and climate-vulnerable states then rejected that weaker draft as too weak.
With finance fights also unresolved, no text could satisfy both sides, so nothing main was adopted.

history.text: A 1992 UN treaty, the UNFCCC, set up yearly climate summits called COPs. The first met in Berlin in 1995, with 117 parties. In 1997 the Kyoto Protocol set binding cuts only for developed countries, averaging 6–8% below 1990 levels for 2008–2012. The US never ratified it. In Copenhagen in 2009, no binding agreement emerged. A short accord, negotiated by about 25 parties, was never formally adopted. Until Antalya, that was the last COP to end with no overarching deal. On 12 December 2015, COP21 adopted the Paris Agreement, which came into force on 4 November 2016. In 2023, COP28's 'UAE consensus' backed transitioning away from fossil fuels. COP30 in Belém in 2025 kept a fossil-fuel roadmap out of its main text. It called for tripling adaptation finance by 2035. It was also the first COP text to admit warming would likely overshoot 1.5C. COP31 fought over the same fossil-fuel wording, and ended without a deal.

lesson.concept: How one country can block a UN climate deal
lesson.big_idea: UN climate summits decide by consensus, not by vote. If even one country objects, the text cannot be adopted, and only earlier agreements stay in force.

steps.title: A COP decides by consensus
steps.text: At a COP, the president can adopt a decision only when no country objects. UN rules require unanimity, so there is no majority vote to fall back on.

steps.title: Drafts are rewritten to avoid objections
steps.text: The presidency writes a draft text and revises it after complaints. But a change made to satisfy one group can push another group away.

steps.title: Every country holds a veto
steps.text: Because one objection is enough, a single country or a bloc can block the whole package. A holdout can win changes just by threatening to object.

steps.title: No deal means old rules stand
steps.text: If nothing is adopted, nothing new starts. Earlier agreements, like the Paris Agreement and the Dubai commitment, still apply, along with separate decisions already passed.

example.result: A big majority is not enough under consensus. When each side objects to the other's text, the summit ends with nothing new adopted, and only old agreements stand.

apply.text: That is COP31. Saudi Arabia and other producers objected to fossil-fuel wording, so the second draft dropped it. The EU, UK and climate-vulnerable states then rejected it as too weak. With objections on both sides, Murat Kurum could not adopt the drafts. The Paris Agreement and the 2023 Dubai commitment still stand.

practice.q: Suppose 20 countries attend. Nineteen accept a text, but one small island state objects because finance is too low. What happens?
practice.answer: Step 1: consensus means every country must accept. Step 2: one objection is enough, so the text is not adopted. Step 3: nothing new begins. Step 4: earlier agreements, like Paris, still apply. A country's size does not matter.

scenes.say: Kaun kya keh raha hai? EU ke Darragh O'Brien ne kaha: hum aisa COP accept nahi karenge jo fossil fuel ko greenwash kare. Saudi Arabia aur dusre producers ne phase-out language ka virodh kiya aur carbon capture and storage ka saath diya, jo carbon dioxide ko zameen ke neeche band kar deta hai. scenes.speak: कौन क्या कह रहा है? thread.previously: The US is tightening routes China uses to reach advanced Nvidia chips. A BIS rule of 16 November requires licences for shipments to five countries and for data centres serving Chinese firms. On 22 November intelligence chief Jay Clayton said China likely found channels and confirmed a probe of ex-Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. The NYT reported a Chinese spy-agency campaign. thread.changed: New on 23 November: Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO, citing senior US government input, days after rejecting his return. Shares jumped 32.2%. Reports add an SEC probe, a California subpoena and a Justice Department smuggling inquiry.

stories.headline: Nvidia's board brings back Jensen Huang days after saying no
stories.question: Why did Nvidia's board reinstate Jensen Huang days after rejecting him, while a spy probe continues?
stories.dek: On 23 November the board said senior US officials had given input and it saw no security risk. President Trump had pushed for his return. Shares jumped 32.2%, but several investigations continue.

so_far.text: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led it for 33 years. On 8 November 2026 he told staff in a memo that he had been unfaithful. The board opened an inquiry into reports that a foreign intelligence service had targeted him. On 12 November Nvidia said he had resigned; some reports give 13 November. Colette Kress, the finance chief, became interim CEO. Days later the board rejected his offer to return. On 22 November intelligence chief Jay Clayton said Washington was investigating an alleged Chinese spy linked to Huang.

what_happened.text: On 23 November 2026 Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. In a filing to US regulators, the board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government. It said it was confident his return poses no national security risk. Colette Kress goes back to being chief financial officer. The board's own investigation into the reported foreign spy effort continues, and Huang pledged to cooperate. The reversal followed President Trump's call for Huang's return. Nvidia shares jumped 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day rise in over two decades.

steps.text: Huang quit on 12 November after admitting he was unfaithful, while reports said a foreign spy service had targeted him.
Days later the board rejected his offer to return. It is not known exactly why it first said no.
Then senior US government officials gave the board input, and it said Huang's return poses no national security risk.
President Trump publicly called for Huang's return, and Fortune reports he pressured the board.
Investors cheered: shares jumped 32.2%, helped, Fortune notes, by a broad rally after major indexes fell into correction the previous week.

history.text:
Nvidia was founded on 5 April 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. It listed its shares on 22 January 1999 and launched the GeForce 256, its first GPU (graphics processing unit, a chip that does many small sums at once). Chips like these later became the engines of artificial intelligence.

That turned them into a security matter. In October 2022 the US restricted exports of high-end chips to China, and Nvidia made the A800 to fit the rules. In October 2023 the curbs widened to lower-performing chips too. Each new rule pushed Nvidia to redesign what it could sell to China. In April 2025 the US required licences for Nvidia's H20 sales to China. In July 2025 it moved to lift that, and Nvidia said it would resume H20 sales. Separately, Nvidia agreed to pay 15% of certain China chip revenue for licences; the sources do not say when.

Investors watched China closely as well. In January 2025 China's DeepSeek AI model surprised them, and Nvidia suffered the largest one-day loss in market value for a US company. Yet it passed $4 trillion in July 2025 and became the first company worth $5 trillion on 29 October 2025.

So in November 2026, when Huang admitted he had been unfaithful and reports said a foreign spy service had targeted him, the worry went beyond his private life. Jay Clayton later called Nvidia chips a 'jewel' everybody wants.

lesson.concept: How a company board hires and removes its CEO
lesson.big_idea: Shareholders own a company, but they elect a board to act for them. Only the board votes to appoint or remove the chief executive, and it can reverse itself when the facts change.

steps.title: Owners elect a board
steps.text: Shareholders own a listed company but cannot run it day to day. So they elect a board of directors to watch over the business on their behalf.

steps.title: The board picks the CEO
steps.text: The board votes to appoint the chief executive, accepts a resignation, or removes the boss. Nvidia's board voted unanimously on 23 November to reinstate Huang, eleven days after announcing his resignation.

steps.title: Independent directors check the boss
steps.text: When the chief executive himself is under question, independent directors, board members who are not employees, investigate. Nvidia's independent-directors committee is still examining reports of a foreign spy effort targeting Huang.

steps.title: Tell investors publicly
steps.text: A US-listed company must announce major events in a public filing called a Form 8-K. Nvidia's board used one to say US government input left it confident of no security risk.

steps.title: The market gives its verdict
steps.text: Share prices show what investors think of the board's choice. Nvidia shares rose 32.2% after the reversal, though Fortune notes a broad market rally also helped.

example.setup: Imagine Crunchy Ltd, a listed snack company whose founder-CEO resigns after a scandal. Its shares trade at ₹100 each.

lines.calc: Founder resigns; finance chief becomes interim CEO

lines.label: Stage 2: first answer
lines.calc: Founder offers to return; board votes no
lines.note: The risk is still unclear, so the board waits.

lines.label: Stage 3: new facts
lines.calc: Authorities tell the board they see no risk
lines.note: The main reason for saying no gets weaker.

lines.label: Stage 4: the vote
lines.calc: Board votes to reinstate; files a public notice
lines.note: Only the board can make this decision.

lines.label: Stage 5: market verdict
lines.note: Investors show they value the founder's return.

example.result: The board, not the shareholders or a politician, makes the formal call, and it can reverse itself when new facts arrive. The share price then shows whether investors agree.

apply.text: That is what happened at Nvidia. After Huang's resignation was announced on 12 November, the board first rejected his return. On 23 November, with input from senior US officials, it voted unanimously to reinstate him and said so in a Form 8-K. Its independent probe keeps running. The 32.2% share jump was investors' verdict, helped by a wider market rally.

practice.q: Say Crunchy's shares were ₹50 before the founder's return and rose 32%. What is the new price? And who could remove the founder again if the probe finds a problem?
practice.answer: 32% of ₹50 = ₹16. New price: ₹50 + ₹16 = ₹66. If the probe finds a serious problem, the board can vote again to remove him, because the board appoints and removes the CEO.

stories.headline: Russia warns Estonia of 'open war' as NATO offers Poland radar plane
stories.question: Is Russia's confrontation with NATO's eastern members edging toward open conflict?
stories.dek: Moscow's warnings are sharper and Russian missiles have landed in Poland. But NATO is answering with surveillance, not force. Its collective-defence trigger needs every ally to agree, and that is seen as unlikely.

so_far.text: Peace efforts have stalled. In September 2026 the Kremlin said talks were on a 'deep pause'. On 19 November 2026 Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen. Their declaration brought no breakthrough on Ukraine, which was not represented. US envoy Jared Kushner said Trump left believing peace is achievable. Overnight on 20 November, during a large Russian attack on Ukraine, missiles and a jet-powered drone came down in south-east Poland. No injuries or damage were reported.

what_happened.text: On 23 November Russia's Foreign Ministry said Estonia was 'on the verge of triggering open war'. It accused Estonia of 'hostile actions' and summoned Estonia's chargé d'affaires, Marek Uhtegi. The same day, after a NATO meeting in Brussels, Polish Deputy Defence Minister Pawel Zalewski said NATO will make an AWACS early-warning aircraft available to Poland. Polish prosecutors now say three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles landed in Poland on 20 November; early reports said two. Also on 23 November, Ukrainian drones hit oil plants in Novoshakhtinsk and in Perm, over 1,420 km from Ukraine.

steps.text: Russia fires large missile and drone waves at Ukraine, and on 20 November some came down in Poland.
Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia, and Moscow accuses Estonia of letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace; Tallinn denies it.
Moscow adds other grievances: obstruction of Russian cargo ships, a grain-transit ban and the treatment of ethnic Russians.
Estonia accuses Russian security services of attempted arson and is shutting its border; Moscow denies it and warns of 'open war'.
Yet responses stay below war: Poland sought surveillance, not Article 4, and Article 5 needs every ally to agree.

history.text: The story starts in 1940. The Soviet Union invaded Estonia on 17 June 1940 and annexed it on 6 August. Estonia restored independence in August 1991, and the last Russian troops left on 31 August 1994. In 2004 Estonia joined NATO and the EU, which placed it under the alliance's protection. In April 2007, moving the Bronze Soldier statue set off a diplomatic row and cyberattacks on Estonian institutions. That showed tension could also be fought online. In March 2014 Russia annexed Crimea and backed militants in Donbas. The 2015 Minsk II deal was never fully implemented. On 24 February 2022 Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Estonia responded with sanctions and expelled diplomats. In October 2022 it recognised Russia as a terrorist state. In January 2023 it expelled 21 Russian staff, and Russia downgraded ties. Then the war began spilling toward NATO. In September 2025 Russian drones entered Polish airspace. Poland invoked NATO's Article 4, which calls for formal consultations, and began preventive air patrols on 17 September 2025. On 20 November 2026 Russian missiles fell in south-east Poland. This time Poland did not invoke Article 4.

lesson.concept: How NATO decides to respond when an ally is hit
lesson.big_idea: NATO does not go to war automatically. Its response climbs a ladder: existing air-guarding missions, then formal talks under Article 4, then collective defence under Article 5, which needs every ally to agree.

steps.title: Rung one: existing missions
steps.text: NATO already runs missions to guard its eastern edge. Poland asked for more help through one, called Eastern Sentry. Extra kit, like an AWACS radar plane that gives allied fighters a shared picture of the sky, comes this way.

steps.title: Rung two: Article 4 talks
steps.text: Any ally that feels threatened can invoke Article 4 of NATO's founding treaty. That means formal consultations: all allies sit down to discuss the threat. Poland did this in September 2025 after Russian drones entered its airspace.

steps.title: Rung three: Article 5 defence
steps.text: Article 5 says an armed attack on one ally counts as an attack on all. It is NATO's war trigger. Using it needs a unanimous political decision, so a single ally saying no can block it.

steps.title: Each ally chooses how to help
steps.text: Even under Article 5, each ally decides what action to take, from sending fighter jets to sending supplies. So the treaty creates a duty to respond, not an automatic war.

apply.text: That is where Poland is now. After Kh-101 missiles landed on 20 November, Poland stayed on rung one. It did not invoke Article 4 and sought help through Eastern Sentry, and NATO will make an AWACS available. Article 5 is seen as unlikely. Russia's warning to Estonia is sharp language, but it is not itself a move up NATO's ladder.

practice.q: Suppose Russian drones cross into an ally's airspace, and that ally asks all NATO members to meet formally. Which rung is that, and does it mean war?
practice.answer: It is rung two, Article 4: a request for formal consultations. Allies talk, but nobody is obliged to act, so it is not war. Moving to Article 5 would need all allies to agree it was an armed attack. Poland did exactly this in September 2025.

Russian troops occupied Crimea... annexed in March 2014; Minsk II February 2015 never fully implemented.

scenes.say: Russia keh raha hai ki Estonia, jo NATO member hai, open war shuru karne ki kagaar par hai. Aur Russian missiles haal hi mein Poland mein gire hain. Toh kya yeh standoff asli jung ki taraf badh raha hai? Chaliye, step by step samajhte hain.
scenes.speak: Russia कह रहा है कि Estonia, जो NATO member है, open war शुरू करने की कगार पर है। और Russian missiles हाल ही में Poland में गिरे हैं। तो क्या यह standoff असली जंग की तरफ बढ़ रहा है? चलिए, step by step समझते हैं।

scenes.say: Pehle nayi khabar. 23 November ko Russia ki Foreign Ministry ne kaha ki Estonia open war shuru karne ki kagaar par hai. Usne Estonia par hostile actions ka ilzaam lagaya. Aur Moscow mein Estonia ke top diplomat, charge d'affaires Marek Uhtegi, ko summon kiya.
scenes.show: Moscow: Estonia 'on the verge' of war
scenes.speak: पहले नई खबर। 23 November को Russia की Foreign Ministry ने कहा कि Estonia open war शुरू करने की कगार पर है। उसने Estonia पर hostile actions का इल्ज़ाम लगाया। और Moscow में Estonia के top diplomat, charge d'affaires Marek Uhtegi, को summon किया।

scenes.say: Ab Poland. 20 November ki raat, Ukraine par ek bade Russian attack ke dauraan, kuch missiles aur ek jet powered drone south east Poland mein gire. Koi zakhmi nahi hua, koi nuksaan nahi hua. Ab prosecutors kehte hain ki wahan 3 Russian Kh 101 cruise missiles gire the. Shuru ki reports mein 2 bataye gaye the.
scenes.speak: अब Poland। 20 November की रात, Ukraine पर एक बड़े Russian attack के दौरान, कुछ missiles और एक jet powered drone south east Poland में गिरे। कोई ज़ख्मी नहीं हुआ, कोई नुकसान नहीं हुआ। अब prosecutors कहते हैं कि वहाँ 3 Russian Kh 101 cruise missiles गिरे थे। शुरू की reports में 2 बताए गए थे।

scenes.say: 23 November ko, Brussels mein NATO meeting ke baad, Poland ke deputy defence minister Pawel Zalewski ne kaha ki NATO Poland ko ek AWACS aircraft dega. Yeh ek udta hua radar plane hai. Usi din Ukrainian drones ne Russia ke kaafi andar, Novoshakhtinsk aur Perm mein oil plants par hamla kiya.
scenes.speak: 23 November को, Brussels में NATO meeting के बाद, Poland के deputy defence minister Pawel Zalewski ने कहा कि NATO Poland को एक AWACS aircraft देगा। यह एक उड़ता हुआ radar plane है। उसी दिन Ukrainian drones ने Russia के काफ़ी अंदर, Novoshakhtinsk और Perm में oil plants पर हमला किया।

scenes.say: Yahan tak pahunche kaise? Shuruaat 1940 se. Soviet Union ne 17 June 1940 ko Estonia par hamla kiya, aur usi August use annex kar liya. Estonia ko apni azaadi wapas August 1991 mein jaake mili. Aakhri Russian troops 31 August 1994 ko gaye.
scenes.speak: यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? शुरुआत 1940 से। Soviet Union ने 17 June 1940 को Estonia पर हमला किया, और उसी August उसे annex कर लिया। Estonia को अपनी आज़ादी वापस August 1991 में जाके मिली। आखिरी Russian troops 31 August 1994 को गए।

scenes.say: 2004 mein Estonia NATO aur European Union mein shaamil hua, yaani alliance ki suraksha mein aa gaya. April 2007 mein Bronze Soldier naam ka ek statue shift kiya gaya. Isse diplomatic jhagda hua aur Estonian institutions par cyberattacks hue.
scenes.speak: 2004 में Estonia NATO और European Union में शामिल हुआ, यानी alliance की सुरक्षा में आ गया। April 2007 में Bronze Soldier नाम का एक statue shift किया गया। इससे diplomatic झगड़ा हुआ और Estonian institutions पर cyberattacks हुए।

Estonia restores independence
Estonia joins NATO and EU

scenes.say: Phir aaya Ukraine. 2014 mein Russia ne Crimea annex kiya aur Donbas mein militants ka saath diya. 2015 ki Minsk 2 deal kabhi poori tarah lagu nahi hui. February 2022 mein full scale invasion hua. Estonia ne sanctions lagaye, Russia ko terrorist state kaha, aur January 2023 mein 21 Russian staff ko nikaal diya. Russia ne rishte downgrade kar diye.
scenes.speak: फिर आया Ukraine। 2014 में Russia ने Crimea annex किया और Donbas में militants का साथ दिया। 2015 की Minsk 2 deal कभी पूरी तरह लागू नहीं हुई। February 2022 में full scale invasion हुआ। Estonia ने sanctions लगाए, Russia को terrorist state कहा, और January 2023 में 21 Russian staff को निकाल दिया। Russia ने रिश्ते downgrade कर दिए।

scenes.say: Phir jung NATO ki taraf phailne lagi. September 2025 mein Russian drones Polish airspace mein ghuse. Poland ne Article 4 invoke kiya, matlab saare allies ke saath formal baatcheet, aur preventive air patrols shuru kiye. Lekin November 2026 mein, jab missiles gire, tab Poland ne aisa nahi kiya.
scenes.speak: फिर जंग NATO की तरफ फैलने लगी। September 2025 में Russian drones Polish airspace में घुसे। Poland ने Article 4 invoke किया, मतलब सारे allies के साथ formal बातचीत, और preventive air patrols शुरू किए। लेकिन November 2026 में, जब missiles गिरे, तब Poland ने ऐसा नहीं किया।

scenes.say: Haal ka silsila: September 2026 mein Kremlin ne kaha ki peace talks deep pause par hain. 19 November ko Trump, Xi aur Putin Shenzhen mein mile, Ukraine ke bina. Koi breakthrough nahi hua. US envoy Jared Kushner ne kaha ki Trump is yakeen ke saath gaye ki peace mumkin hai.
scenes.speak: हाल का सिलसिला: September 2026 में Kremlin ने कहा कि peace talks deep pause पर हैं। 19 November को Trump, Xi और Putin Shenzhen में मिले, Ukraine के बिना। कोई breakthrough नहीं हुआ। US envoy Jared Kushner ने कहा कि Trump इस यकीन के साथ गए कि peace मुमकिन है।

scenes.say: Toh yeh garmi badh kyun rahi hai? Pehla, Russia Ukraine par missiles aur drones ki badi waves chalata hai, aur kuch Poland mein gire. Doosra, Ukraine Russia ke andar door tak hamla karta hai, aur Moscow ka ilzaam hai ki Estonia Ukrainian drones ko apna airspace use karne deta hai. Estonia isse inkaar karta hai.
scenes.show: Strays into Poland; drones over Estonia?
scenes.speak: तो यह गर्मी बढ़ क्यों रही है? पहला, Russia Ukraine पर missiles और drones की बड़ी waves चलाता है, और कुछ Poland में गिरे। दूसरा, Ukraine Russia के अंदर दूर तक हमला करता है, और Moscow का इल्ज़ाम है कि Estonia Ukrainian drones को अपना airspace use करने देता है। Estonia इससे इनकार करता है।

scenes.say: Teesra, Moscow ki aur bhi shikaayatein hain: Russian cargo ships ko rokna, grain transit par ban, aur ethnic Russians ke saath bartaav. Chautha, Estonia Russian security services par arson ki koshish ka ilzaam lagata hai, jisse Russia inkaar karta hai, aur apna border band kar raha hai. Jawab mein Moscow aur zor se warnings deta hai.
scenes.show: Grievances pile up on both sides
scenes.speak: तीसरा, Moscow की और भी शिकायतें हैं: Russian cargo ships को रोकना, grain transit पर ban, और ethnic Russians के साथ बर्ताव। चौथा, Estonia Russian security services पर arson की कोशिश का इल्ज़ाम लगाता है, जिससे Russia इनकार करता है, और अपना border बंद कर रहा है। जवाब में Moscow और ज़ोर से warnings देता है।

scenes.say: Phir bhi, jawab jung se neeche hi reh rahe hain. Poland ne zyada surveillance maangi, Article 4 talks nahi. Aur NATO ka war trigger, Article 5, tabhi chalta hai jab har ek ally raazi ho.
scenes.speak: फिर भी, जवाब जंग से नीचे ही रह रहे हैं। Poland ने ज़्यादा surveillance माँगी, Article 4 talks नहीं। और NATO का war trigger, Article 5, तभी चलता है जब हर एक ally राज़ी हो।

scenes.say: Ab players. NATO ke Secretary General Mark Rutte kehte hain ki alliance Estonia aur Poland par nazar rakh raha hai aur uske paas jawab dene ke options hain. Donald Tusk Poland ke Prime Minister hain. Poland ke deputy defence minister Pawel Zalewski ne radar plane ka announcement kiya. Aur war warning Russia ki Foreign Ministry ne di.
scenes.speak: अब players। NATO के Secretary General Mark Rutte कहते हैं कि alliance Estonia और Poland पर नज़र रख रहा है और उसके पास जवाब देने के options हैं। Donald Tusk Poland के Prime Minister हैं। Poland के deputy defence minister Pawel Zalewski ने radar plane का announcement किया। और war warning Russia की Foreign Ministry ने दी।

scenes.say: Ab numbers. NATO ke paas 14 AWACS radar planes hain, jo Germany mein based hain. 2022 se yeh NATO ke eastern flank par nazar rakh rahe hain, aur allied fighters ko ek shared radar picture dete hain. Inmein se ek Poland ko diya ja raha hai.
scenes.speak: अब numbers। NATO के पास 14 AWACS radar planes हैं, जो Germany में based हैं। 2022 से यह NATO के eastern flank पर नज़र रख रहे हैं, और allied fighters को एक shared radar picture देते हैं। इनमें से एक Poland को दिया जा रहा है।

scenes.say: Agla number: 1420 kilometre se zyada. Perm refinery Ukraine se itni door hai, phir bhi drones wahan pahunch gaye. Yeh saal mein lagbhag 13 million tonne process kar sakti hai. Ukraine ki military kehti hai ki 3 key units hit hui, lekin nuksaan verify nahi hua hai.
scenes.speak: अगला number: 1420 kilometre से ज़्यादा। Perm refinery Ukraine से इतनी दूर है, फिर भी drones वहाँ पहुँच गए। यह साल में लगभग 13 million tonne process कर सकती है। Ukraine की military कहती है कि 3 key units hit हुईं, लेकिन नुकसान verify नहीं हुआ है।

scenes.say: Ab is sab ke peeche ka idea: jab kisi ally par hamla ho, toh NATO kaise jawab deta hai. Woh automatically jung mein nahi kudta. Uska jawab ek ladder chadhta hai. Rung 1: existing missions, jaise Eastern Sentry. Extra madad, jaise radar plane, isi raaste aati hai.
scenes.speak: अब इस सब के पीछे का idea: जब किसी ally पर हमला हो, तो NATO कैसे जवाब देता है। वो automatically जंग में नहीं कूदता। उसका जवाब एक ladder चढ़ता है। Rung 1: existing missions, जैसे Eastern Sentry। Extra मदद, जैसे radar plane, इसी रास्ते आती है।

scenes.say: Rung 2: NATO ki founding treaty ka Article 4. Jo bhi ally khatra mehsoos kare, woh formal consultations bula sakta hai, jahan saare allies saath baithte hain. Sirf baatcheet, action nahi. Poland ne September 2025 mein yahi kiya tha.
scenes.speak: Rung 2: NATO की founding treaty का Article 4। जो भी ally खतरा महसूस करे, वो formal consultations बुला सकता है, जहाँ सारे allies साथ बैठते हैं। सिर्फ़ बातचीत, action नहीं। Poland ने September 2025 में यही किया था।

scenes.say: Rung 3: Article 5. Ek ally par armed attack, sab par attack maana jaata hai. Yeh NATO ka war trigger hai, aur ise use karne ke liye unanimous political decision chahiye. Uske baad bhi har ally khud tay karta hai ki woh kya action lega. Toh yeh jawab dene ki zimmedaari hai, automatic jung nahi.
scenes.speak: Rung 3: Article 5। एक ally पर armed attack, सब पर attack माना जाता है। यह NATO का war trigger है, और इसे use करने के लिए unanimous political decision चाहिए। उसके बाद भी हर ally खुद तय करता है कि वो क्या action लेगा। तो यह जवाब देने की ज़िम्मेदारी है, automatic जंग नहीं।

scenes.say: Maan lijiye Country A, ek NATO member, ko ek khet mein missile ke tukde milte hain. Koi zakhmi nahi. Pehla sawaal: missile kiski hai, jaan boojhkar aayi ya bhatak kar? Rung 1: existing missions se zyada madad. Rung 2: Article 4 talks. Rung 3 ke liye har ally ko maanna hoga ki yeh attack tha. Ek bhi na, aur yeh ruk jaata hai. Toh ek harmless stray missile aksar Rung 1 ya 2 par hi ruk jaati hai.
scenes.show: Walk a stray missile up the ladder
scenes.speak: मान लीजिए Country A, एक NATO member, को एक खेत में missile के टुकड़े मिलते हैं। कोई ज़ख्मी नहीं। पहला सवाल: missile किसकी है, जान बूझकर आई या भटक कर? Rung 1: existing missions से ज़्यादा मदद। Rung 2: Article 4 talks। Rung 3 के लिए हर ally को मानना होगा कि यह attack था। एक भी ना, और यह रुक जाता है। तो एक harmless stray missile अक्सर Rung 1 या 2 पर ही रुक जाती है।

scenes.say: Ab alag alag raay. Russia ki Foreign Ministry kehti hai ki Estonia open war shuru karne ki kagaar par hai, aur uska border band karna zaroor ulta padega. Estonia inkaar karta hai ki usne apni zameen use hone di. Poland ke Donald Tusk missiles ko jaan boojhkar kiya gaya provocation kehte hain. NATO ke Rutte ise grave violation kehte hain. Donald Trump ne ishaara kiya ki missiles galti se gire.
scenes.speak: अब अलग अलग राय। Russia की Foreign Ministry कहती है कि Estonia open war शुरू करने की कगार पर है, और उसका border बंद करना ज़रूर उल्टा पड़ेगा। Estonia इनकार करता है कि उसने अपनी ज़मीन use होने दी। Poland के Donald Tusk missiles को जान बूझकर किया गया provocation कहते हैं। NATO के Rutte इसे grave violation कहते हैं। Donald Trump ने इशारा किया कि missiles गलती से गिरे।

Denies letting its territory be used for drone attacks
The missiles were an intentional provocation
The missiles landed in Poland 'by mistake'

scenes.say: Ek aam galatfehmi: NATO desh mein missile gire, toh automatic jung. Aisa nahi hai. Aur India? Hamare sources yahan kisi asar ki baat nahi karte, isliye hum nahi keh sakte ki prices, jobs ya travel par kya farak pad sakta hai. Haan, yeh ladder Poland ko samjhata hai: Article 4 nahi, Eastern Sentry ke zariye madad, aur ek radar plane. Article 5 ko unlikely maana ja raha hai.
scenes.speak: एक आम ग़लतफ़हमी: NATO देश में missile गिरे, तो automatic जंग। ऐसा नहीं है। और India? हमारे sources यहाँ किसी असर की बात नहीं करते, इसलिए हम नहीं कह सकते कि prices, jobs या travel पर क्या फ़रक पड़ सकता है। हाँ, यह ladder Poland को समझाता है: Article 4 नहीं, Eastern Sentry के ज़रिए मदद, और एक radar plane। Article 5 को unlikely माना जा रहा है।

scenes.say: Kya dekhna hai: 1 December ko Estonia Russia ke saath apne border crossings band kar raha hai, Narva samet, kam se kam 6 mahine ke liye. Abhi tak pata nahi: missiles Poland mein jaan boojhkar aaye ya nahi, radar plane ud raha hai ya nahi, Russia border ko lekar jawabi karvai karega ya nahi, aur peace talks dobara kab shuru ho sakti hain.
scenes.speak: क्या देखना है: 1 December को Estonia Russia के साथ अपने border crossings बंद कर रहा है, Narva समेत, कम से कम 6 महीने के लिए। अभी तक पता नहीं: missiles Poland में जान बूझकर आए या नहीं, radar plane उड़ रहा है या नहीं, Russia border को लेकर जवाबी कार्रवाई करेगा या नहीं, और peace talks दोबारा कब शुरू हो सकती हैं।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. NATO ka jawab ek ladder hai, aur Article 5 ke liye har ally ki haan chahiye. Russia ne Estonia ko open war ki warning di, lekin NATO ne Poland ke missiles ka jawab radar plane se diya, force se nahi. Aur 1 December par nazar rakhiye, jab Estonia apne Russia border crossings band karega.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। NATO का जवाब एक ladder है, और Article 5 के लिए हर ally की हाँ चाहिए। Russia ने Estonia को open war की warning दी, लेकिन NATO ने Poland के missiles का जवाब radar plane से दिया, force से नहीं। और 1 December पर नज़र रखिए, जब Estonia अपने Russia border crossings बंद करेगा।

stories.headline: DRC's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases, with no approved vaccine
stories.question: Why is this Ebola outbreak spreading faster than any before, and can it be stopped?
stories.dek: It is Bundibugyo, an Ebola strain with no approved vaccine or drug, spreading undetected through a war zone with weakened health services. Vaccine trials began in October, and results are expected in early 2027.

so_far.text: Ebola is a virus that spreads through the body fluids of sick or dead people. On 15 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared a new outbreak after lab sequencing identified Bundibugyo virus, a rarer Ebola species. The virus probably jumped to people in early 2026, months earlier. Within days, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern. Cases passed 1,000 on 20 June, 5,000 on 23 August and 10,000 on 27 October. On 21 August, UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said the outbreak was growing exponentially and outpacing the response.

what_happened.text: WHO's latest update, published on 20 November 2026, counted 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths in DRC as of 17 November. That is a death rate of 48.9%, almost one in two. Cases span 68 health zones in eight provinces, mostly in Ituri and North Kivu in the east. On 18 November, WHO reconfirmed the global emergency. It says transmission remains sustained and high, though some areas show a slight decline. On 21 November, heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri disrupted the response. Health workers sheltered in a maternity ward for over 24 hours.

steps.text: This is Bundibugyo virus, not Zaire, so the vaccine and treatments that helped in 2018–2020 were not made for it.
It spread undetected from an estimated early-2026 spillover until the 15 May declaration, starting many chains of infection.
With no approved vaccine, teams rely on tracing contacts, but only 81% are seen daily, against a 95% target.
Fighting, displacement and infections in clinics add cases, while 2025 aid cuts weakened surveillance and unpaid health workers went on strike.
Each missed case starts new chains, so cases multiply: 1,000 on 20 June, 10,000 by 27 October.

history.text:
Ebola was first identified in 1976 at Yambuku, in what was then Zaire and is now DRC. That outbreak had 318 cases and 280 deaths. A separate outbreak hit southern Sudan the same year.

In August 2007, a different species, Bundibugyo virus, was found in Uganda's Bundibugyo District. That outbreak had 149 cases and 37 deaths, about one in four. DRC had its own Bundibugyo outbreak in 2012, with 77 cases and 36 deaths.

The biggest turning point came in 2013–2016. In West Africa, Ebola went unrecognised for months and reached capital cities such as Conakry, Monrovia and Freetown. It became the largest epidemic ever: 28,616 infections and 11,310 deaths. After it, a vaccine called rVSV-ZEBOV (sold as Ervebo) appeared protective in a trial announced in December 2016. It was approved in 2019. But it targets the Zaire strain only.

From 2018 to 2020, Ebola struck North Kivu and Ituri, the same eastern provinces hit in 2026. About 70 armed groups were active there, and nearly 400 attacks on health workers were reported by January 2020. Still, about 300,000 people were vaccinated, and the outbreak totalled 3,470 cases.

In 2025, the US dismantled its aid agency, USAID, and froze aid. That weakened DRC's health and disease-tracking systems, and unpaid health workers went on strike several times. So when Bundibugyo returned in 2026, it met a conflict zone, a weaker health system and no vaccine.

Bundibugyo virus discovered in Uganda: 149 cases, 37 deaths

items.meaning: More than three times the 2018–2020 Kivu outbreak (3,470); West Africa 2013–16 had 28,616.
Share of confirmed cases who died, almost one in two; Uganda's 2007 outbreak killed about one in four.

analogy.text: Think of a forest fire. Each burning tree can light others nearby. Firefighters win by watching the trees around each blaze and wetting them, which is like ring vaccination. In DRC there is no proven spray yet, only four in five nearby trees get checked each day, and some areas are too dangerous to enter.
analogy.breaks: Trees stay put. People travel, and can carry the virus for days before falling ill, so new fires start far away.

for_you.text: The direct risk in India is small. India has reported no Bundibugyo cases, and WHO rates the risk as low for most countries. Since 21 May 2026, airports have screened arrivals from DRC, Uganda and South Sudan, and India advises avoiding non-essential travel there. Since 25 June, all international travellers must file a health self-declaration on the Air Suvidha 2.0 portal before arrival.

misconception.myth: There is already an Ebola vaccine, so this outbreak should be easy to control.
misconception.fact: The approved vaccine, Ervebo, targets the Zaire strain. No vaccine or treatment is approved for Bundibugyo; Ervebo and two new candidates are only being tested.

next.text: Watch the Tumaini trial in Bunia. WHO advisers want Oxford's and Moderna's vaccines added once national approvals come, and results are expected in early 2027. Kenya and Nigeria are in 42-day countdowns to be declared over. Watch whether slight declines in some areas hold.

lesson.concept: How an outbreak grows, and how it is stopped
lesson.big_idea: Every outbreak turns on one number: how many people each sick person infects. Above one, cases multiply round after round. Below one, each round is smaller and the outbreak dies out.

steps.title: Count who each case infects
steps.text: Scientists call the average number of people one sick person infects the reproduction number, or R. If R is 2, each case leads to two more.

steps.title: Cases come in generations
steps.text: One round of infection is a generation. Each generation is the last one multiplied by R. So growth is multiplication, not addition. That is what 'exponential' means.

steps.title: One is the tipping point
steps.text: If R is above 1, each generation is bigger and the outbreak grows. If R drops below 1, each generation is smaller, and the chains of infection die out.

steps.title: Breaking chains lowers R
steps.text: Health workers lower R by tracing contacts, checking them daily and isolating anyone who falls ill. WHO's target is to see 95% of contacts daily. Ring vaccination, protecting the circle around each case, lowers R further.

steps.title: What pushes R up
steps.text: Missed cases, infections inside clinics, deaths in the community, fighting that keeps teams out, and having no vaccine all keep R high. WHO lists all of these in DRC.

example.setup: Imagine an outbreak with 100 cases. Assume each sick person infects 2 others, and a new generation appears every two weeks. Then health workers improve tracing.

lines.label: Generation 1
lines.note: Assume each case infects two people within two weeks

lines.label: Generation 2
lines.note: The new cases pass it on too

lines.label: Generation 3
lines.note: Eight times bigger in six weeks: exponential growth

lines.label: Tracing cuts R to 0.8
lines.note: Assume most contacts are now caught and isolated early

lines.label: Next generation
lines.note: Smaller each round, so chains start dying out

example.result: Doubling turned 100 cases into 800 in six weeks. Pushing R just below 1 did not stop cases at once, but it turned growth into steady decline.

apply.text: DRC's outbreak shows this multiplication. Cases passed 1,000 on 20 June, 5,000 on 23 August and 10,000 on 27 October. With no approved vaccine, teams rely mainly on tracing, and they see only 81% of contacts daily, not 95%. Fighting, like that near an Ituri hospital on 21 November, pushes R back up. The Tumaini trial aims to add ring vaccination.

practice.q: Suppose an outbreak has 100 cases and each case infects 1.5 people per generation. How many new cases after three generations?
practice.answer: Multiply by 1.5 each generation. 100 × 1.5 = 150. 150 × 1.5 = 225. 225 × 1.5 = 337.5, about 338. Cases more than triple in three rounds, because R is above 1.

check.q: If better tracing means each Ebola case infects fewer than one person on average, what happens?
options: Cases still double, just more slowly
Each round of cases is smaller, so the outbreak shrinks
All new cases stop at once
check.why: Below one, each generation is smaller than the one before, so chains die out over time, not instantly.

takeaways: An outbreak grows when each case infects more than one person, and shrinks below one.

scenes.speak: 2018 से 2020 तक Ebola ने Ituri और North Kivu को मारा। वहाँ लगभग 70 armed groups active थे, और health workers पर क़रीब 400 हमले report हुए। फिर भी लगभग 3 लाख लोगों को vaccine लगी। फिर 2025 में United States ने अपनी aid agency, USAID, ख़त्म कर दी, और DRC के health systems कमज़ोर हो गए।

scenes.speak: यह outbreak 15 May 2026 को declare हुआ, जब lab sequencing में Bundibugyo virus मिला। शायद यह महीनों पहले ही इंसानों तक पहुँच चुका था। WHO ने कुछ ही दिनों में global emergency declare कर दी। 21 August तक UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis ने कहा कि यह exponentially बढ़ रहा है, response से भी तेज़।

scenes.say: Toh itna tez kyun? Pehli wajah, strain. 2018 se 2020 mein jo vaccine aur treatments use hue, woh Zaire ke liye bane the, Bundibugyo ke liye nahi. WHO kehta hai ki Bundibugyo ke liye koi approved vaccine ya specific treatment nahi hai.
scenes.speak: तो इतना तेज़ क्यों? पहली वजह, strain। 2018 से 2020 में जो vaccine और treatments use हुए, वो Zaire के लिए बने थे, Bundibugyo के लिए नहीं। WHO कहता है कि Bundibugyo के लिए कोई approved vaccine या specific treatment नहीं है।

scenes.say: Doosri wajah, head start. Yeh mahinon tak chupchaap faila aur kai chains shuru ho gayi. Vaccine ke bina sabse bada tool hai contact tracing: patient jin logon ke paas tha, un sabko har din check karna. WHO ka target hai 95 percent contacts. Pahunch hai sirf 81 percent tak.
scenes.speak: दूसरी वजह, head start। यह महीनों तक चुपचाप फैला और कई chains शुरू हो गईं। Vaccine के बिना सबसे बड़ा tool है contact tracing: patient जिन लोगों के पास था, उन सबको हर दिन check करना। WHO का target है 95 percent contacts। पहुँच है सिर्फ़ 81 percent तक।

scenes.say: Teesri wajah, halaat. Ladai aur displacement ki wajah se teams pahunch nahi paati. Log clinics ke andar infect ho jaate hain, aur kai log community mein hi mar jaate hain, khaaskar chhote bachche. 2025 ke aid cuts ne health systems kamzor kiye, aur bina salary wale health workers strike par chale gaye. Har chhoota hua case nayi chain shuru karta hai, isliye cases badhte jaate hain.
scenes.speak: तीसरी वजह, हालात। लड़ाई और displacement की वजह से teams पहुँच नहीं पातीं। लोग clinics के अंदर infect हो जाते हैं, और कई लोग community में ही मर जाते हैं, ख़ासकर छोटे बच्चे। 2025 के aid cuts ने health systems कमज़ोर किए, और बिना salary वाले health workers strike पर चले गए। हर छूटा हुआ case नई chain शुरू करता है, इसलिए cases बढ़ते जाते हैं।

scenes.say: Isme kaun kaun shaamil hai? Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus ki leadership mein WHO ne emergency phir se confirm ki. UN ke Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis ne August mein exponential growth ki warning di. Oxford aur Moderna ne candidate vaccines banayi. Africa CDC kehta hai ki 2 point 9 billion dollar ka vaada hua, lekin aadhe se kam paisa hi mila.
scenes.speak: इसमें कौन कौन शामिल है? Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus की leadership में WHO ने emergency फिर से confirm की। UN के Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis ने August में exponential growth की warning दी। Oxford और Moderna ने candidate vaccines बनाईं। Africa CDC कहता है कि 2 point 9 billion dollar का वादा हुआ, लेकिन आधे से कम पैसा ही मिला।

scenes.say: Ab numbers dekhiye. Cases 20 June ko 1000 paar hue, 23 August ko 5000, aur 27 October ko 10000. 10 hazaar se 11 hazaar tak pahunchne mein sirf 12 din lage. 21 August tak maut ka aankda 2500 paar kar chuka tha, aur inme se aadhi pichhle 20 dinon mein hui thi.
scenes.speak: अब numbers देखिए। Cases 20 June को 1000 पार हुए, 23 August को 5000, और 27 October को 10000। 10 हज़ार से 11 हज़ार तक पहुँचने में सिर्फ़ 12 दिन लगे। 21 August तक मौत का आँकड़ा 2500 पार कर चुका था, और इनमें से आधी पिछले 20 दिनों में हुई थीं।

scenes.say: Ab pichhle outbreaks se compare kijiye. 2018 se 2020 ke Kivu outbreak mein 3470 cases the. Yeh outbreak usse 3 guna se bhi zyada bada hai. West Africa, jo ab tak ka sabse bada tha, usme atthais hazaar chhe sau cases the, yaani woh phir bhi isse lagbhag dhaai guna bada hai.
scenes.speak: अब पिछले outbreaks से compare कीजिए। 2018 से 2020 के Kivu outbreak में 3470 cases थे। यह outbreak उससे 3 गुना से भी ज़्यादा बड़ा है। West Africa, जो अब तक का सबसे बड़ा था, उसमें अट्ठाईस हज़ार छह सौ cases थे, यानी वो फिर भी इससे लगभग ढाई गुना बड़ा है।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jisse sab samajh aa jaayega. Har outbreak ek number par tika hai: ek beemar insaan average mein kitne logon ko infect karta hai. Ise kehte hain R, reproduction number. Infection ka har round pichhle round ko R se multiply karta hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो एक idea जिससे सब समझ आ जाएगा। हर outbreak एक number पर टिका है: एक बीमार इंसान average में कितने लोगों को infect करता है। इसे कहते हैं R, reproduction number। Infection का हर round पिछले round को R से multiply करता है।

scenes.say: Agar R 1 se upar hai, toh har round bada hota hai aur outbreak badhta hai. 1 se neeche, toh har round chhota hota hai aur chains khatam ho jaati hain. Tracing, isolation aur ring vaccination, matlab har case ke aas paas ke ghere ko bachana, R ko neeche laate hain. Chhoote hue cases, clinic infections aur ladai ise upar dhakelte hain.
scenes.speak: अगर R 1 से ऊपर है, तो हर round बड़ा होता है और outbreak बढ़ता है। 1 से नीचे, तो हर round छोटा होता है और chains ख़त्म हो जाती हैं। Tracing, isolation और ring vaccination, मतलब हर case के आस पास के घेरे को बचाना, R को नीचे लाते हैं। छूटे हुए cases, clinic infections और लड़ाई इसे ऊपर धकेलते हैं।

scenes.say: Maan lijiye 100 cases hain. Assume kijiye har beemar insaan har do hafte mein 2 aur logon ko infect karta hai. Do hafte baad: 200. Chaar hafte baad: 400. Chhe hafte baad: 800. Chhe hafte mein 8 guna. Yahi hai exponential growth.
scenes.speak: मान लीजिए 100 cases हैं। Assume कीजिए हर बीमार इंसान हर दो हफ़्ते में 2 और लोगों को infect करता है। दो हफ़्ते बाद: 200। चार हफ़्ते बाद: 400। छह हफ़्ते बाद: 800। छह हफ़्ते में 8 गुना। यही है exponential growth।

scenes.say: Ab tracing R ko ghata kar zero point aath kar deti hai. 800 guna zero point aath hua 640. Phir 640 guna zero point aath hua 512. Cases ek dum se gayab nahi hote, lekin har round chhota hota jaata hai.
scenes.speak: अब tracing R को घटा कर ज़ीरो point आठ कर देती है। 800 गुना ज़ीरो point आठ हुआ 640। फिर 640 गुना ज़ीरो point आठ हुआ 512। Cases एक दम से ग़ायब नहीं होते, लेकिन हर round छोटा होता जाता है।

scenes.say: India ke liye iska kya matlab hai? Seedha khatra kam hai; India mein Bundibugyo ka koi case report nahi hua. 21 May 2026 se airports par DRC, Uganda aur South Sudan se aane walon ki screening ho rahi hai, aur India wahan bina zaroorat travel na karne ki salah deta hai. 25 June se international travellers ko ek online health form bharna hota hai, Air Suvidha two point oh.
scenes.speak: India के लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? सीधा ख़तरा कम है; India में Bundibugyo का कोई case report नहीं हुआ। 21 May 2026 से airports पर DRC, Uganda और South Sudan से आने वालों की screening हो रही है, और India वहाँ बिना ज़रूरत travel न करने की सलाह देता है। 25 June से international travellers को एक online health form भरना होता है, Air Suvidha two point oh।

scenes.say: Ek aam myth: Ebola ki vaccine toh hai, toh yeh aasaan hona chahiye. Asal mein Ervebo Zaire strain ko target karti hai; Bundibugyo ke liye kuch bhi approved nahi hai. Isliye teams tracing par tiki hain, aur roz 81 percent contacts tak pahunch rahi hain, 95 tak nahi. WHO DRC mein risk ko very high maanta hai, zyadatar deshon ke liye low.
scenes.show: Myth: a vaccine already works here
scenes.speak: एक आम myth: Ebola की vaccine तो है, तो यह आसान होना चाहिए। असल में Ervebo Zaire strain को target करती है; Bundibugyo के लिए कुछ भी approved नहीं है। इसलिए teams tracing पर टिकी हैं, और रोज़ 81 percent contacts तक पहुँच रही हैं, 95 तक नहीं। WHO DRC में risk को very high मानता है, ज़्यादातर देशों के लिए low।

scenes.say: Kya ise roka ja sakta hai? Kuch ilaakon mein halki giravat dikh rahi hai. Uganda ka outbreak 28 July ko khatam declare hua, aur Kenya aur Nigeria 42 din ke countdown mein hain. 23 October ko Bunia mein Tumaini trial shuru hua, jo ring vaccination ke saath Ervebo ko Bundibugyo ke khilaaf test kar raha hai.
scenes.speak: क्या इसे रोका जा सकता है? कुछ इलाक़ों में हल्की गिरावट दिख रही है। Uganda का outbreak 28 July को ख़त्म declare हुआ, और Kenya और Nigeria 42 दिन के countdown में हैं। 23 October को Bunia में Tumaini trial शुरू हुआ, जो ring vaccination के साथ Ervebo को Bundibugyo के ख़िलाफ़ test कर रहा है।

scenes.say: 4 November ko WHO ke advisers ne Oxford aur Moderna ki vaccines ko bhi jodne ki salah di, national approvals milne par. Results 2027 ki shuruaat mein aane ki ummeed hai. Drug trials July mein shuru hue; is strain ke liye koi bhi licensed nahi hai. Abhi tak pata nahi: koi vaccine kaam karti hai ya nahi, giravat tikegi ya nahi, aur kaunsi wajah sabse zyada maayne rakhti hai.
scenes.speak: 4 November को WHO के advisers ने Oxford और Moderna की vaccines को भी जोड़ने की सलाह दी, national approvals मिलने पर। Results 2027 की शुरुआत में आने की उम्मीद है। Drug trials July में शुरू हुए; इस strain के लिए कोई भी licensed नहीं है। अभी तक पता नहीं: कोई vaccine काम करती है या नहीं, गिरावट टिकेगी या नहीं, और कौनसी वजह सबसे ज़्यादा मायने रखती है।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Ek: outbreak tab badhta hai jab har case ek se zyada logon ko infect karta hai. Do: DRC ka Bundibugyo outbreak gyarah hazaar chhe sau cases paar kar chuka hai, aur koi approved vaccine nahi hai. Teen: Tumaini trial par nazar rakhiye, jiske results 2027 ki shuruaat mein aane ki ummeed hai.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। एक: outbreak तब बढ़ता है जब हर case एक से ज़्यादा लोगों को infect करता है। दो: DRC का Bundibugyo outbreak ग्यारह हज़ार छह सौ cases पार कर चुका है, और कोई approved vaccine नहीं है। तीन: Tumaini trial पर नज़र रखिए, जिसके results 2027 की शुरुआत में आने की उम्मीद है।

thread.previously: On 20 November 2026, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a claimed Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis and its generalisation, released as Lean code in 14 packages. MIT's Andrew Sutherland compiled it. Maynard is '98 or 99 percent' certain; Conrad called the release outrageous. A comparator check of the Lean statement is pending, and no human-readable version exists. A rival human draft by Masullo, shared by Vakil, was found to have problems.
thread.changed: New since 20 November: the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative certified the proof on 21 November; comparison tools confirmed the statement matches; checkers nanoda and con-leche accepted it; Clay still lists it unsolved.

stories.headline: Independent checkers back AI-assisted Riemann proof; no human understands it yet
stories.question: Has an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis really been verified?
stories.dek: By computers, largely yes: several independent checkers accepted the code, and the groups behind Lean certified it. By people, not yet: nobody understands it, and the $1 million prize still waits.

so_far.text: On 20 November 2026, Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic, posted a note on his website. It claimed a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, made with help from Anthropic's AI, Claude. The proof was not written in ordinary maths language. It was released as code in Lean, a computer language that checks proofs step by step. The code runs to about 17 million lines. The open question was whether the code's statement truly matched the famous problem.

what_happened.text: On 21 November 2026 the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative, groups behind Lean and its shared maths library Mathlib, issued a joint statement. It certified that both the statement and the proof are correct. Two independent comparison tools confirmed the theorem's conclusion matches Mathlib's existing statement of the hypothesis. Two separately written proof checkers, nanoda and con-leche, accepted the full proof, including a wider version for Dirichlet L-functions. MIT's Andrew Sutherland rebuilt it offline; it matched byte for byte. Yet on 22 November the Clay Mathematics Institute still listed the problem as unsolved.

steps.text: Lean accepts a proof only if its small core program, the kernel, confirms every step follows from basic rules called axioms.
Here the kernel and two separately written checkers all accepted the proof, using only three standard axioms, so a hidden error is very unlikely.
But a checker only confirms the statement as typed; a mistranslated statement would prove the wrong theorem.
Two comparison tools found the conclusion matches Mathlib's existing Riemann statement, which closes that gap.
Machine checking is not human acceptance: nobody yet understands the proof, and Clay needs publication, two years and general acceptance.

history.text: The story begins in 1859. Bernhard Riemann was studying how many prime numbers lie below a given size. He used a formula now called the zeta function, which has special points called zeros. He wrote that it was very probable all the important zeros lie on one line, the critical line. That guess is the Riemann hypothesis. In 1896 Hadamard and de la Vallée-Poussin proved no zeros lie on a neighbouring boundary line. That was the key step in proving the prime number theorem, which describes how primes thin out. In 1900 David Hilbert put Riemann's guess on his famous list of problems for the new century. In 1914 Hardy proved that infinitely many zeros lie on the critical line, though not that all do. Around 1940 Weil proved a version for a simpler setting, curves over finite fields. In 2000 the Clay Mathematics Institute made it one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, each worth $1 million. Computers later checked the first 12 trillion zeros, and all lie on the line. But examples cannot cover infinitely many zeros, so that is not a proof. In August 2026 Anthropic said an unreleased Claude raised the proven share of zeros on the line from 41.6% to 67.2%. It said those techniques would not prove the hypothesis itself. Three months later came Alpöge's claim.
