lesson.concept: How a computer checks a mathematical proof
lesson.big_idea: A proof tool like Lean checks every step mechanically. Trust then rests on three things: the statement says the right thing, the checker is sound, and only standard axioms are used.

steps.title: Write the proof as code
steps.text: In Lean, each step of a proof is written as code. Mathlib is a shared library of maths already checked this way, so new proofs can build on it.

steps.title: A small kernel checks steps
steps.text: Lean's kernel is a small core program. It accepts a step only if it follows from earlier steps and basic rules called axioms. Sutherland says only three standard axioms were used here.

steps.title: Check the statement too
steps.text: The kernel only checks the statement as typed. If the code states something subtly different, it proves the wrong theorem. So comparison tools check the statement against a trusted version.

steps.title: Recheck with independent checkers
steps.text: A bug in one checker could let an error slip through. So separately written checkers, like nanoda and con-leche, rerun the proof. If all agree, a hidden error is very unlikely.

steps.title: Checked is not understood
steps.text: A checked proof shows a result is true, not why. People still need a readable explanation, and prize bodies like Clay demand publication and general acceptance.

example.setup: Imagine a student, Asha, writes a 1,000-line Lean proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers, and enters it in a maths competition.

lines.label: Stage 1: the statement
lines.calc: Asha types: for every number, a bigger prime exists
lines.note: This is exactly what the code will prove.

lines.label: Stage 2: compare it
lines.calc: A tool matches it to Mathlib's trusted version
lines.note: Catches a slip that would change the claim.

lines.label: Stage 3: kernel check
lines.calc: Kernel accepts all 1,000 lines, standard axioms only
lines.note: Every step follows from the basic rules.

lines.label: Stage 4: second opinions
lines.calc: Two independent checkers also accept all 1,000 lines
lines.note: Makes a hidden bug in Lean's own kernel very unlikely.

lines.label: Stage 5: explain it
lines.calc: Judges ask Asha to explain the key idea
lines.note: Checking shows it is true; explaining shows why.

example.result: If Stages 1 to 4 pass, the proof is almost certainly correct. But the judges still want Stage 5, an explanation people can follow, before they award a prize.

apply.text: Alpöge's proof has passed Stages 1 to 4. Comparison tools matched its statement to Mathlib's; the kernel, nanoda and con-leche accepted it; Sutherland's rebuild matched byte for byte. Stage 5 is missing. Buzzard says nobody yet understands what it shows, Rubinstein's guide still relies on Lean for a central inequality, and Clay lists the problem unsolved.

practice.q: Suppose every checker accepts every step, but the comparison tool finds the code's statement differs from Mathlib's. Has the Riemann hypothesis been proved?
practice.answer: No. Step 1: the checkers confirm the steps, so the code proves its own statement. Step 2: that statement is not the trusted version of the hypothesis. Step 3: so the code proves something else. The statement match is what links the code to the real problem.

check.q: Why did mathematicians like Kevin Buzzard care whether the Lean statement matched Mathlib's existing one?
options: A checker only confirms what the code states, so a mistranslated statement would prove the wrong theorem
Mathlib's version is shorter, so the proof runs faster
Clay pays its prize only for proofs written in Lean
check.why: The kernel guarantees the steps, not that the typed statement is the famous problem. The comparison tools close that gap.

takeaways: A computer checker confirms every step; trust also needs the right statement and independent checkers.
The Claude-assisted Riemann proof has passed independent machine checks, but no human yet understands it.
Watch for a human-readable write-up, journal publication, and Clay's two-year wait before any prize.

sources.excerpt: Alpöge made the claim in a note on his website on Friday, November 20, 2026 (per Bloomberg's Nov 21 report); 'I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.'
Buzzard asked "what is the statement of the theorem in the Lean code." Comparator looks for tampering such as redefined symbols; the update says it "has now been completed."
The Lean and Mathlib communities placed the target theorem in a separate challenge file that imported only Mathlib. Two comparison tools confirmed the conclusion matched Mathlib's existing statement.
1859: Bernhard Riemann first posed the hypothesis in his paper on the number of primes less than a given magnitude; 'very probable that all roots are real'.
Hilbert presented it at the 1900 Paris congress; Hardy (1914) showed infinitely many zeros lie on the critical line.
The Clay Mathematics Institute made it one of seven prize problems, each worth $1 million.
Raised the known lower bound... from 41.6% to 67.2%... Anthropic does not expect the techniques to prove the Riemann hypothesis itself. Lean formalization passes the comparator tool.

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? Alpoge mathematicians ke liye ek write-up plan kar rahe hain; abhi koi nahi hai. Raw export par Sutherland ke apne runs ab bhi chal rahe the. Phir koi publication, aur Clay ka do saal ka wait. Pata nahi: kya Clay ise accept karega, aur Anthropic ki August wali post ne kyun kaha ki uske methods hypothesis prove nahi karenge.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? Alpoge mathematicians के लिए एक write-up plan कर रहे हैं; अभी कोई नहीं है। Raw export पर Sutherland के अपने runs अब भी चल रहे थे। फिर कोई publication, और Clay का दो साल का wait। पता नहीं: क्या Clay इसे accept करेगा, और Anthropic की August वाली post ने क्यों कहा कि उसके methods hypothesis prove नहीं करेंगे।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Ek: checker har step confirm karta hai, lekin bharose ke liye sahi statement aur independent checkers bhi chahiye. Do: Claude ki madad wala Riemann proof independent machine checks pass kar chuka hai, lekin abhi koi insaan ise samajhta nahi. Teen: readable write-up, publication aur Clay ke do saal ke wait par nazar rakhiye.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। एक: checker हर step confirm करता है, लेकिन भरोसे के लिए सही statement और independent checkers भी चाहिए। दो: Claude की मदद वाला Riemann proof independent machine checks pass कर चुका है, लेकिन अभी कोई इंसान इसे समझता नहीं। तीन: readable write-up, publication और Clay के दो साल के wait पर नज़र रखिए।

The transfer fails
The bank decides instead

quiz.q: The repo rate is 5.50% and October inflation was 6.1%. Why does that point towards another hike?
options: The real rate is below zero, so borrowing is still cheap
Inflation is safely inside the RBI's 2–6% band
A hike automatically raises FD rates by the same amount
quiz.why: 5.50% minus 6.1% is about −0.6%. Money is cheap in real terms, so a hike pushes the real rate up and cools spending.

quiz.q: A portal asks for your OTP, then shows any Form 6 whose number you type. What is missing?
options: Authentication: proving who you are
Authorisation: checking the form belongs to you
A faster server
quiz.why: The OTP already proves who you are. The missing step is checking that the requested record is yours, so strangers' forms load.
